To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

in ischemic areas significantly decreased high-energy phosphate compounds and increased lactate, pyruvate contents were found in comparison to both control hearts and to nonischemic parts of infarct hearts, and in ischemic areas mitochondrial Mg2+-ATPase activity was decreased, whereas in nonis-chemic regions of infarct heart increased mitochondrial ATPase activity could be observed.

ischemia causes a significant decrease of high-energy phosphate content, an increase of lactate and pyrvate contents, and a decrease of mitochondrial ATPase activity in the ischemic areas of the infarcted myocardium.
ischemic and non-ischemic areas of myocardium with experimental coronary occlusion differ in the levels of energy-rich compounds and mitochondrial Mg2+-activated ATPase activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the interrelationship between changes of high-energy phosphate and mitochondrial ATPase activity in ischemic and in nonischemically working areas of the left heart ventricle with experimental infarction.
a possible role of mitochondrial ATPase in the pathogenesis of ischemic injury of the myocardium.

a possible relationship between changes in the levels and turnover of high-energy phosphate and changes in the activity of mitochondrial Mg-2+ plus-stimulated adenylate kinase in ischemic and in nonischemically affected areas of the myocardial infarct.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the drop in Mg2+ stimulated mitochondrial ATPase activity in ischemic regions may be the cause of the observed changes in high-energy phosphate content in these areas.
a decrease in the activity of mitochondrial Mg-2-plus-stimulated ATP-ase in the ischemic area is associated with an increase of the activity in the nonischaemic area.

the decrease in Mg2+-dependent ATPase activity in ischemic areas of the infarcted heart may be due to a decrease in the levels of Mg2+ and/or ATP, and/or due to a direct inhibitory effect of lactate on the enzyme activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the changes in the high-energy phosphate compounds and in the activity of mitochondrial ATPase are interdependent and reflect the metabolic state in the myocardium.

a drop in Mg2+ stimulated mitochondrial ATPase activity in ischemic areas is associated with a decrease in the content of high-energy phosphate, whereas in nonis- chemic areas the increase in ATPase activity is accompanied by increased contents of high-energy phosphate and FFA.

a drop in the activity of Mg2+-stimu-lated mitochondrial ATPase in the ischemic area is a consequence of the decreased content of high-energy phosphates and that the increase in activity in non-ischemic areas is a compensatory reaction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the changes in mitochondrial Mg2+-activated ATPase activity and high-energy phosphate compounds are interrelated and may serve as a marker of the ischemic state in the heart.
changes in the activity of mitochondrial ATPase are closely related with changes in the high-energy phosphate compounds.
the mitochondrial Mg2+-ATPase may be a good marker of the ischemic state of the myocardium.
